title: MLOps
blurb: Take models to production and keep them healthy: tracking, pipelines, feature stores, serving, safe rollouts, drift monitoring and governance.

quiz.question: What is training/serving skew?
options: Features computed differently in training and production, so the model sees different inputs live
quiz.explanation: Prevent it with shared feature definitions (feature store) and monitoring served feature distributions.

quiz.question: What should a model registry alias such as "champion" enable?
options: Promotion and rollback as metadata changes with an audit trail
quiz.explanation: Serving loads models by alias, so switching versions does not require code changes.

quiz.question: In a shadow deployment, the new model…
options: Scores real traffic but its predictions are not used
quiz.explanation: Shadow mode compares behaviour and latency with zero user risk.

quiz.question: A PSI of 0.32 on a key feature indicates…
quiz.explanation: Rule of thumb: <0.1 stable, 0.1–0.25 moderate, >0.25 significant.

quiz.question: Which drift can only be fully confirmed once ground-truth labels arrive?
quiz.explanation: Input distributions can look unchanged while the relationship to the target shifts.

quiz.question: Why pin library versions in the serving image to match training?
options: Different versions can change predictions or fail to load the model
quiz.explanation: Serialisation formats and numerical behaviour can differ across versions.

problems.title: Notebook to production
problems.prompt: Take a notebook churn model to production.
problems.solution: Refactor into a pipeline (extract, validate, features, train, evaluate with slice gates, register), choose batch weekly scoring with idempotent partition writes and model version per row, sync to CRM, monitor drift, score distribution and realised churn, and retrain through the same gated pipeline.

problems.title: Safe model rollout
problems.prompt: Roll out a new fraud model with minimal risk.
problems.solution: Pass offline gates, run shadow on live traffic comparing predictions and latency, canary 5% with automated rollback on error/latency/distribution alerts, A/B the business metric, then full rollout keeping the previous version warm.
